correctness.rationale: For cubic G=C_n square K_2, the edge-component identity 2|S|-n=c(G-S)+e_G(S) provides the lower bound floor(n/2)+1. No adjacent empty columns are possible. Isolated empty columns reduce foresthood to at least one disrupted rail chain, while a double column breaks the chain. Classifying possible empty/single/double column runs at equality yields three disjoint even cases and one odd case. Their exact rail assignments prove n 2^m and n(3m+2)2^(m-2). For odd n>=7, m-1 rung flips plus two independent conditional horizontal slides yield the 1:2:1 degree law; n=3,5 are separately proved. A DSU edge-checking enumerator reproduced every optimum n=3..12, and independent sliding checker reproduced all degrees n=3,5,7,9,11. These tests are finite corroboration only.

value.rationale: This is a natural all-length finite-graph family with an already studied minimum decycling number and algorithmic interest in optimum-set reconfiguration. Counting ALL optimum feedback sets, unlike demonstrating the minimum deletion size, exposes parity-dependent exponential solution multiplicity, with a different structural mechanism at even and odd sizes. The exact odd-slide degree distribution quantifies the availability of local repairs at each optimum, a finer invariant not implied by unrestricted exchange connectivity. It provides reproducible test instances for exact enumeration and constrained reconfiguration algorithms, not an arbitrary slice of instances.
